title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: Pork sausages baked in crisp Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: Plump pork sausages baked inside a crisp, puffed, deeply savoury Yorkshire pudding batter. One of the great British comfort dishes, served with onion gravy and mashed potato.

recipe.sourceNotes: Toad in the hole is a traditional British dish in which sausages are baked in Yorkshire pudding batter. The name is first recorded in the eighteenth century, though the exact origin of the term is unclear: the most common explanation is that the sausages, half-visible in the risen batter, resemble toads peering out of a hole. Historically the dish was made with any cheap meat, including offal; pork sausages became the standard filling during the nineteenth century. The batter is identical to Yorkshire pudding batter: a simple mixture of eggs, flour, and milk or a mixture of milk and water, rested before cooking and poured into a smoking-hot tin with fat in the bottom. The key to the batter rising to a crisp, hollow-sided result is the fat being hot enough to begin cooking the batter immediately on contact. The dish is traditionally served with onion gravy.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin approximately 30 x 20 cm, or a round cast-iron skillet.

content.text: The most important rule: the fat in the tin must be smoking hot before the batter goes in. Take the tin out of the oven with the sausages already browned in it, place it on the hob over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the fat is shimmering and smoking, then pour the batter in quickly and get it back into the oven immediately. Do not open the oven door for the first 20 minutes. Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes before cooking if you have time.

items.preparation: optional; leaves stripped and stirred into the batter

content.text: Make the batter: sift the flour and salt into a bowl. Make a well in the centre, crack in the eggs, and whisk together. Add the milk gradually, whisking to a smooth batter the consistency of double cream. Rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Put the oil in the roasting tin and heat in the oven for 5 minutes. Add the sausages and cook for 15 minutes, turning once, until browned.

Remove the tin from the oven. Heat on the hob over high heat until the fat is smoking. Pour in the batter immediately. Return to the oven at once. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes without opening the door until the batter is well risen, golden, and crisp at the edges. Serve immediately with onion gravy.
